```cicada
song { main*16 }
fx tone eq { type = highpass frequency = 25Hz q = 0.707 }
fx glue comp { threshold = -18dB ratio = 2 makeup = 1dB }
fx punch transient { attack = 2dB sustain = -1dB }
fx stereo width { amount = 1.08 bass_mono = 100Hz }
fx ceiling limiter { ceiling = -1dBTP lookahead = 3ms release = 100ms }
master { insert = tone -> glue -> punch -> stereo -> ceiling }
export broadcast { loudness = -23LUFS true_peak = -1dBTP normalize = off }
```

Run `cicada render score.cicada --export broadcast --bars 16 -o broadcast.wav`.
The export target uses the existing iterative BS.1770 loudness renderer and
measures the delivered WAV. Live playback does not apply programme normalization.
An unreachable target returns an error instead of claiming success. This
one-track bass cannot reach a −14 LUFS streaming target, because the renderer
adds at most 12 dB of input gain, so the example asks for the −23 LUFS
broadcast level.

### Export loudness targets

A loudness target (`--loudness`, or an `export` block with `loudness`) renders
the score in up to six passes. Each pass measures the delivered WAV and adjusts
one static gain. Where that gain goes depends on the master chain.

| Master chain | Where the gain goes | What holds the true-peak ceiling |
| --- | --- | --- |
| No limiter | Direct renderer: after the master chain. Scheduled renderer (arrangements, audio clips, serial track effects, sample packs): at the master input, as in earlier releases, because the engine applies its master gain before the chain. Output is unchanged from earlier releases. | The gain stops at the ceiling. It keeps crest factor, so an ambitious target can miss and returns a shortfall error. |
| Contains a `limiter` | At the master input: after the music and SFX buses sum and the master `level`, before the chain. | Your limiter. The extra level reaches it, so it reduces peaks and a punchy mix can get louder than its natural crest allows. |

Without a limiter, a target that the render misses at the true-peak ceiling
ends its error with the fix: add a limiter at the export's true-peak ceiling
as the last master insert, such as `fx ceiling limiter { ceiling = -1dBTP }`
with `master { insert = ceiling }`. `cicada render --json` reports it as the
code `loudness_shortfall_at_true_peak_ceiling` with a `remedy` that holds the
exact score text for that score and ceiling, and the `addeffect` intent that
makes the same change with `cicada apply`
([agent formats](docs/manual/agents.md#render---json)).

With a limiter in the chain, the renderer keeps two guard rails:

- Input gain is capped at +12 dB.
- The chain limiter's gain reduction is held to 6 dB or less. Ordinary
  streaming masters use a few dB of limiting; 6 dB is the upper end.

A target that needs more than either limit stops short and returns a shortfall
error that names the limit that bound. The WAV from the best pass is still
written (Studio keeps it as a separate shortfall file). When even a render
that breaks a limit is too quiet for the target, and the best render is within
0.5 dB of the reduction maximum, the search stops instead of using all six
passes. The render summary reports the applied gain, the gain stage (`master_input` when the gain runs ahead of the master chain, `post_chain` when it runs after it or there is no chain), the
chain limiter's largest gain reduction, and the largest gain reduction of any
limiter. Review these numbers and run `cicada verify-wav` on the result.

Only the first pass synthesizes the mix, on both renderers and with or without
a master chain. It stores the signal that enters the master stage (the summed
buses, before the master `level` and the export gain) in a temporary file next
to the output, and later passes play that signal back through the master
gain, the chain and the safety limiter with the new gain. A pass whose gain
differs from an earlier pass's by less than the renderer's gain can show is not
rendered at all: it reuses that pass's audio and measurement. The result
matches rendering every pass in full, byte for byte. The render summary counts
the full syntheses, the cached replays and the repeated passes, and lists each
pass's gain, loudness and true peak. `CICADA_RENDER_NO_REUSE=1` turns the reuse
off, so every pass synthesizes the song (see the [CLI reference](docs/cli.md)).

The file takes about 23 MB per minute at 48 kHz, counted from the start of the
song to the end of the exported range plus its tail, so an export of the last
bars of a long song stores the whole song up to them. It stays until the export
ends, on the same disk as the export's two other temporary WAV files (one holds
the pass being rendered, the other the best pass so far). On a nearly full disk
it can take space that those files need, so the export frees it as follows:

- If the export cannot create the file, or a write to it fails, it renders every
  pass in full.
- If a pass, or the copy of a pass to the best-pass file, fails while the file
  exists, the export deletes the file, repeats that step without it, and renders
  every later pass in full. A pass fails when its render, its sync to disk or its
  close fails, or when the stored signal cannot be read back.
- If the repeated step fails too, the export stops with that error.

Passes rendered without the file take longer, but the WAV and the report are the
same.

The same renderer serves `cicada render --export`, `--loudness`, and Studio's
export. `cicada stems` does not apply loudness targets. The built-in safety
limiter (ceiling -0.3 dBFS) still follows the chain in both modes.

| Kind | Controls (defaults; ranges) |
| --- | --- |
| `eq` | `type = peak` (`peak`, `low_shelf`, `high_shelf`, `highpass`, `lowpass`); `frequency = 1000Hz` (10 Hz to 0.45 × render rate); `q = 1` (0.1–20); `gain = 0dB` (−24 to +24 dB). Declare separate EQ effects for multiple bands. |
| `comp` | Existing compressor controls: `threshold`, `ratio`, `knee`, `attack`, `release`, `makeup`, `detect`, `mix`. Master compression detects its own stereo input. |
| `transient` | `attack = 0dB`, `sustain = 0dB` (−18 to +18 dB); `fast = 1ms` (0.1–10 ms), `slow = 30ms` (10–100 ms, greater than fast), `release = 120ms` (20–1000 ms). |
| `width` | `amount = 1` (0–2); `bass_mono = 0Hz` (bypass, or 20–500 Hz). |
| `limiter` | `ceiling = -1dBTP` (−12 to 0 dBTP); `lookahead = 3ms` (1–10 ms); `release = 100ms` (20–1000 ms). |
| `convolution` | Required `asset` name; `mix = 0.15` (0–1); `partition = 128frames` (power of two, 64–2048). See [score impulses](docs/audio/convolution.md#score-impulses). |

The chain accepts at most 16 distinct effect names, in any order. Processing and
reset allocate no memory. Offline export removes the summed processor latency
and drains delayed final samples. Omission or `insert = none` preserves legacy
output. Tracks accept eight serial inserts; the music bus still accepts one compressor. Master effects have
fixed controls until recompilation; scene settings and live parameter paths for
them are rejected. A compressor cannot share state between music and master.

Prepared processors cannot be encoded into a core WASM project image. Browser
score playback needs the companion modules connected by its host; that wiring
is separate from native playback and Studio's saved-chain display. The master companion remains separate from core track processing.


## Track inserts

Track inserts accept up to eight distinct named stages in authored order.
Supported kinds are `drive`, `eq`, `comp`, `deesser`, `ampcab`, and `chorus`. Each track owns separate
filter and detector state. The chain runs before the fader and both send taps,
so vocal reverb and delay receive the processed voice. All processing and resets
allocate no memory. The engine aligns tracks to the longest drive-insert delay;
EQ, compression, and de-essing add no latency.

```cicada
cicada 2
fx cleanup eq { type = highpass frequency = 80Hz q = 0.707 }
fx leveler comp { threshold = -18dB ratio = 3 makeup = 0dB }
fx sibilance deesser { frequency = 6000Hz threshold = -24dB ratio = 4 range = 9dB }
track lead piano { insert = cleanup -> leveler -> sibilance }
pattern phrase { 1 . 3 . 5 . 3 . }
scene main { lead = phrase }
song { main*4 }
```

The same chain can be inserted on recorded `audio` tracks. Add one EQ declaration
per band; track EQ frequency is 10–19845 Hz, with the same type, Q, and gain
controls as master EQ. Track compressors detect their own stereo input and do
not accept an external sidechain. Saved chain edits rebuild independent state;
scene and live effect automation on a serial track chain are currently rejected.
The legacy single-drive insert retains its live controls. A track with exactly
one chorus also exposes `chorus_rate`, `chorus_depth`, `chorus_spread`, and
`chorus_mix` for scene settings, automation, and modulation routes.

The stereo chorus uses one to three voices. `rate` is 0.05–5 Hz (default
0.6 Hz), `depth` is 0–8 ms (default 3 ms), and `spread` and `mix` are 0–1
(defaults 1 and 0.5). `voices` is an integer from 1 to 3 (default 3). The
four continuous controls use a 10 ms smoother. Settled `mix = 0` passes the
dry signal exactly while maintaining the delay history.

```cicada
cicada 2
fx wide chorus { voices = 3 rate = 0.6Hz depth = 3ms spread = 1 mix = 0.5 }
track lead acid { insert = wide }
pattern phrase { 1 . 3 . }
lfo drift { wave = triangle rate = 2bars }
mod drift -> lead.chorus_mix depth = 0.25
scene main { lead = phrase }
song { main*4 }
```

Browser and WAM playback select the optional modular kernel for chorus. Portable
chorus projects have a conservative 8 MiB effect-working-storage limit;
externally prepared master processors cannot yet be included in that budget.

The stereo-linked de-esser uses a complementary first-order split: it attenuates
the high-frequency band while retaining the vocal body. `range` caps detector
gain reduction; it does not guarantee that every frequency is attenuated by
that amount. Set `mix = 0` for exact bypass.

| De-esser control | Unit | Range | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `frequency` | Hz | 2000–12000 | 6000 |
| `threshold` | dBFS (write `dB`) | −60–0 | −24 |
| `ratio` | unitless | 1–20 | 4 |
| `range` | dB | 0–24 | 9 |
| `attack` | ms | 0.1–20 | 1 |
| `release` | ms | 10–500 | 80 |
| `mix` | unitless | 0–1 | 1 |

Studio's **Add vocal chain** creates an 80 Hz highpass, a compressor at −18 dB
with ratio 3 and zero makeup, and the default de-esser in one undoable save. It
keeps existing inserts and leaves an existing EQ → compressor → de-esser trio
unchanged. Adjust the threshold to the recorded signal; these defaults are a
starting point, not automatic leveling. Finish an active take before saving
Mixer changes.

Native playback, export, and portable playback use the same saved track stages.
Core images require `TrackEffectsCapability` (bit 11). Studio automatically loads
`cicada-vocals.wasm` for those images; scores using modeled keyboard voices load
`cicada-keys.wasm`, which also includes track processing. The default portable
core rejects the track-processing requirement. Missing optional modules return
an error instead of silently playing without the effects.

Build the optional processing variant with `make build-vocals-wasm`. Its raw and
Brotli bytes are reported separately; the default core retains the 322 KiB raw
and 120 KiB Brotli gates. WAM2 export automatically packages the required variant
from beside the configured core file. `make build-wam2` prepares both the core
and vocal modules; modeled keys require `make build-keys-wasm`.

## Tape echo

`tape` is a delay return that behaves like a tape echo. Declare it where you
would declare a `delay`, send tracks to it the same way, and a score has one
delay return: either `delay` or `tape`.

```cicada
cicada 2
tempo 74
fx echo tape { time = 3/16 feedback = 0.6 wow = 0.5 flutter = 0.2 saturation = 0.4 damp = 3200Hz }
track rim drums { send echo = 0.8 pre }
pattern hit drums { rs: x... .... .... .... }
automate echo.time { @1.1.1 608ms @3.1.1 300ms smooth }
scene main { rim = hit }
song { main*4 }
```

In this score the repeats start at 608 ms and, over two bars, slow their
spacing down to 300 ms. The pitch of the repeats rises while the time shortens
and falls while it lengthens, as it does when you turn the delay knob on a tape
machine.

| Control | Unit | Range | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `time` | note division or ms | 1/32 up to 2 s, 1 ms to 2000 ms | 1/8 |
| `feedback` | unitless | 0–0.95 | 0.4 |
| `wow` | unitless | 0–1 | 0.4 |
| `flutter` | unitless | 0–1 | 0.2 |
| `saturation` | unitless | 0–1 | 0.3 |
| `damp` | Hz | 1000–16000 | 5000 |

All six controls take scene settings (`echo.feedback = 0.3`) and `automate`
lanes (`echo.time`, `echo.wow`, `echo.flutter`, `echo.feedback`,
`echo.saturation`, `echo.damp`). Each moves through a 5 ms smoother, except
`time`, which glides as described below.

**What it models.**

- One read head over a 2-second stereo buffer. A change of `time`, from
  automation, a scene, or a tempo change on a synced time, moves the head at up
  to half a sample per sample, so the repeats play between 0.5x and 1.5x speed
  during the move. Nothing crossfades. A jump of 300 ms takes 0.6 s.
- Wow: slow drift of the head (two sines near 0.37 and 1.3 Hz), up to 3 ms of
  excursion at `wow = 1`. Flutter: fast ripple (near 7 and 11 Hz), up to 0.25 ms
  at `flutter = 1`.
- A one-pole `damp` filter and a `tanh` limiter inside the feedback loop.
  `saturation` drives that limiter harder and divides the drive back out, so
  quiet repeats keep the `feedback` gain and loud repeats compress.
- With `wow`, `flutter` and `saturation` at 0, `tape` matches a stereo `delay`
  that has the same time, feedback and `damp`, no ping-pong, width 1 and mix 1.
  The match is byte for byte when the time is a whole number of frames. For
  other times it differs by float rounding, under -120 dB.

**What it does not model.** There is no tape-head frequency response, no
hiss, no bias or print-through, and no motor inertia beyond the fixed glide
rate. There is no ping-pong, width or mix control: the return is always
wet-only and stereo-preserving. It cannot be a track insert or a master stage.
Modulation routes to its controls are not supported yet. Portable browser kernel
images refuse a score that declares `tape`, with a clear error; native playback
and offline `render` and `stems` support it.

## Same bits on every machine

**The rule.** A score renders to the same bits on amd64 (any CPU and any
`GOAMD64` level), arm64 and WebAssembly, from voice to exported file. Two
things in Go can break it. Fusion is ruled out everywhere on that path; the
math library is not yet, so part of it matches in the tests without being
guaranteed.

- **Fused multiply-add.** Go may compute `x*y + z` with one rounding instead
  of two on arm64 and with `GOAMD64=v3`. What is guaranteed: the compiler
  reports no product it would fuse in `kernel/`, `render/` and the packages
  `render` imports, on arm64 and with `GOAMD64=v3` (CI builds them with
  `-d=fmahash=vy` and fails on any report). A product is rounded with an
  explicit `float32(...)` or `float64(...)`, for example `a + float64(b*c)`.
  Go may also fuse across statements, so a conversion of a plain value is
  needed where that value is itself a product: a variable set from a product
  in an earlier statement (`s1 := state*inv` then `float64(g*u) + float64(s1)`),
  a parameter of a function the compiler inlines into a caller that passes a
  product, and `v` in `2*v`, which the compiler rewrites as `v + v`. Elsewhere
  such a conversion prevents nothing and is left out; the compiler's report
  decides which are needed.
  Not yet covered: `cmd/cicada` (live monitor mixing in
  `studio_audio_devices.go`) and the `host/` packages that `render` does not
  import; a later pull request in this series extends the check to every
  package that produces audio a user hears, records or exports.
- **Math library functions.** `math.Exp`, `math.Log`, `math.Pow`, `math.Sin`
  and the others can differ in the last bit by target: `math.Exp` even uses an
  FMA instruction only on amd64 CPUs that have one. Every processor in
  `kernel/fx` and its subpackages (the master EQ, compressor, limiter,
  transient shaper, width, room and normalizer, the convolution FFT, and the
  track effects: amp and cabinet, chorus, compressor, de-esser, delay, drive,
  reverb and tape), the mix in `kernel/mix`, the loudness meter and the export
  gain use `kernel/dsp/detmath` instead, whose functions return the same bits
  everywhere and are within 1 ULP of the exact result. Still on the math
  library: the engine (master gain, parameter smoothing), automation curves,
  the graph interpreter, vibrato, spatial audio and the voices; each such file
  is listed with its exact count in the source guard below.

The follow-up removes the rest: no architecture-dependent `math` call
between voice and exported file, and a digest per processor and voice on all
three targets.

**How to check it.**

```
go test -count=1 ./kernel/dsp/detmath ./kernel/fx/... ./kernel/mix ./kernel/loudness
```

pins each processor's output as a SHA-256 digest; CI runs the same tests on
arm64 and with `GOAMD64=v3`. To list fusable expressions, build for arm64 with
the compiler's FMA report:

```
GOARCH=arm64 go build -gcflags='m31labs.dev/cicada/...=-d=fmahash=vy' ./kernel/... ./render/...
```

Each `fmahash triggered FILE:LINE` line is a product that arm64 fuses; CI fails
on any. `TestRenderPathAvoidsMathLibrary` in `kernel/dsp/detmath` reads every
Go file in `kernel/` and `render/`, the loudness search in
`cmd/cicada/main.go` and the automation curves in `project/automation.go`, and
fails on any `math` function outside a short list of exact ones (`Sqrt`,
`Abs`, `Floor`, `Ldexp`, bit conversions and the like). Files that still call
the others are listed with their exact count, so a new call fails; analysis
code that never produces audio (`kernel/analysis`, `render/fingerprint.go`) is
exempt.

The exported file itself is compared too. `TestExampleWAVParity` in
`cmd/cicada` runs `cicada render` on example scores four ways (plain,
`--normalize`, -14 LUFS / -1 dBTP, -9 LUFS / -1.5 dBTP) and hashes each WAV:

```
CICADA_WAV_PARITY_OUT=$PWD/build/wav-hashes.txt go test ./cmd/cicada -run '^TestExampleWAVParity$' -count=1 -v
CICADA_WAV_PARITY_REFERENCE=$PWD/build/wav-hashes.txt go test ./cmd/cicada -run '^TestExampleWAVParity$' -count=1 -v
```

The first command writes the hashes (CI runs it on amd64), the second compares
another machine's renders with them (CI runs it on arm64). Pull requests
render a subset; the nightly run sets `CICADA_WAV_PARITY_ALL=1` and renders
every score under `examples/`. A render known to differ is listed, with the
date and the cause, in `knownWAVDifferences`; the list can only shrink.

# Parameter ranges

Every voice, drum, effect and master-chain setting has an allowed range. `cicada check`,
`render`, Studio and the language server report each setting that is outside it, at
the setting's own value. A message names the setting, the value as you wrote it, and
the range:

```text
main.cicada:4:14: error CICADA-PARAM: drums oh_decay 50ms is below the minimum 150ms (range 150ms to 1.2s)
```

Scene settings and automation points that set the same parameters use the same
wording. Each stage reports all of its errors in one run, but a stage runs only when the
one before it is clean: scene settings are checked while the score is read, then track
and effect declarations, then automation points. Fix the errors from one stage and run
again to see the next. Limits are shown to six significant digits, rounded toward the inside of
the range. Mixer settings (`level`, `pan`, sends) are described in the
[edition 1 specification](docs/spec/edition-1.md#track-mixer-settings).

## Piano (`track name piano`)

| Setting | Unit | Minimum | Maximum | Also accepts |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `sustain` | unitless | 0 | 1 |  |

## Drums, bass drum (`track name drums`)

| Setting | Unit | Minimum | Maximum | Also accepts |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `bd_tune` | Hz | 40Hz | 120Hz |  |
| `bd_decay` | ms or s | 80ms | 1.5s |  |
| `bd_sweep` | unitless | 1 | 8 |  |
| `bd_sweep_time` | ms or s | 10ms | 80ms |  |
| `bd_click` | unitless | 0 | 1 |  |
| `bd_drive` | unitless | 0 | 1 |  |

# docs/manual/diagnostics.md

# Diagnostic codes

<!-- Generated from internal/diagnostics/catalog.go. Do not edit; run
CICADA_UPDATE_DIAGNOSTICS_DOC=1 go test ./internal/diagnostics -run TestDiagnosticsReferenceIsCurrent -->

Every code cicada can report, with its severity, where it is reported, what
it means and how to fix it. `cicada diagnostics` prints the same list, and
`cicada diagnostics --json` writes it as JSON ([agent formats](docs/manual/agents.md#diagnostics---json)).
A test fails when the code emits a code this list lacks.

Where a code is reported:

- **score**: validating a score. `cicada check` prints it with its source line,
  `cicada check --json` gives its position as data, and `validate`, `render` and
  the language server report it too.
- **command**: the error of a command, such as `lib`, `bundle`, `convert`,
  `director` or the export settings of `render`.
- **studio**: responses of Studio, the browser host or the public demo.
- **edit**: refusals of edit intents, from `cicada apply` and Studio.

| Code | Severity | Where | Meaning | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `CICADA-ARRANGEMENT` | error | score | an arrange block is invalid: it is used together with a song block or in an edition-1 score; it has no placements; a placement or marker has an unknown field, lacks at (or a placement its length), has a malformed or out-of-range time, or a time whose source and typed values differ; a placement's ID is invalid, its content has no track slot, its pattern does not suit its track, or a step pattern placement starts between steps | use arrange in an edition-2 score without a song block, give it at least one placement, give each placement at and length and each marker at as musical times inside the song (such as @5.1.1 and 2bars), use only those fields, place patterns on tracks of their kind, and start step patterns on a step (check --json offers a moveclip fix for that one) |
| `CICADA-ASSET-FORMAT` | error | score | an audio asset's declared format, frames, rate or channels are invalid or differ from the WAV file | declare format = wav and the file's real frames, rate (8000 to 384000 Hz) and channels (1 or 2); the message gives the expected and actual values |
| `CICADA-ASSET-HASH` | error | score | an audio asset's sha256 is malformed or does not match the file's bytes | write the file's SHA-256 as 64 lowercase hex digits in quotes, or restore the file the score pinned |
| `CICADA-ASSET-MISSING` | error | score | an audio asset's file, or the project or library folder it lives in, cannot be read | put the file at the declared path, relative to the folder of cicada.mod (or of the score when there is none) |
| `CICADA-ASSET-PATH` | error | score | an audio asset's path leaves the project folder, or a library asset is not under audio/ | use a project-relative path without .. that stays inside the project; library assets live under audio/ |
| `CICADA-AUDIO` | error | studio | browser audio is not ready for the request: transport stopped, worklet send failed, or a reset is pending | start browser audio and the transport, or wait for the fresh worklet kernel image after Stop, then retry |
| `CICADA-CAPABILITY` | error | studio | the public demo session does not offer this command | use the command in a local cicada studio session |
| `CICADA-CHAIN` | error | score | a track's chain names no patterns or more than 32 | give the chain 1 to 32 pattern names |
| `CICADA-CLIP-RANGE` | error | score | an audio clip's region, gain or fades are invalid, or a clip is bound to a track that is not an audio track | use start < end within the asset in frames, s or ms that resolve to whole frames, gain -60 to +24 dB, fades no longer than the region, and bind clips to audio tracks |
| `CICADA-DEMO` | error | studio | the public demo host refused its build or request (missing source commit, unsupported host, bad asset or entry document) | build the demo from a full source commit and serve it from a supported host |
| `CICADA-DIRECTOR` | error | score, command | the live block cannot become a Game Director manifest: an invalid state or stinger name, or a stinger pattern without a track slot | use valid identifiers for states and stingers and bind each stinger pattern to a track slot |
| `CICADA-DUPLICATE` | error | score | a name is declared twice in one namespace, or uses a reserved name; the message names the first declaration | rename or remove one of the declarations |
| `CICADA-EXPANSION` | error | score | a pattern expands beyond 64 steps after its phrase uses | use fewer or shorter phrase uses, or split the pattern |
| `CICADA-EXPERIMENTAL` | error | score | an experimental voice (guitar) is used without opting in | add experimental = on to the track |
| `CICADA-GRID` | error | score | a step grid attribute or tuplet group is invalid: tuplets need 2 to 8 pitches that divide a cell into whole ticks of at least 30 | use a supported step division and tuplet sizes |
| `CICADA-HISTORY` | error | studio | the public demo session has no change to undo or redo | make a change first |
| `CICADA-IO` | error | score, command | a file cannot be read, or has an extension the command does not accept | check the path and pass a .cicada score (or .json where the command says so) |
| `CICADA-KEY` | error | score | the key root or scale is unknown | use a root such as a, c# or eb and a scale: minor, major, dorian, phrygian, harmonic, mixo, pent or blues |
| `CICADA-LIB-ASSET` | error | command | convert cannot write library-owned audio into semantic JSON | keep the score's imports, or vendor the library, until asset vendoring is supported |
| `CICADA-LIB-CAPABILITY` | error | score | an imported library requires an engine edition or capability this cicada does not support | update cicada or use a library version that fits it |
| `CICADA-LIB-CYCLE` | error | score | libraries import each other in a cycle | remove one import of the cycle the message names |
| `CICADA-LIB-DECL` | error | score | a library declares something only a score may declare, or a qualified name | keep tracks, scenes, songs and other score-only declarations in the score; library names are unqualified |
| `CICADA-LIB-HASH` | error | score, command | an imported library is not pinned in cicada.sum, or its content differs from the pin | run cicada lib update <path> after an intended change; vendoring refuses a library that changed while it copied |
| `CICADA-LIB-IMPORT` | error | score | a score with imports was parsed without the project source loader | check the score as a file (cicada check score.cicada) so imports resolve |
| `CICADA-LIB-MISSING` | error | score | an imported library is not found in std, the project lib/ folder or the user library | run cicada lib list to see what resolves; create, vendor or fix the import path |
| `CICADA-LIB-PATH` | error | score, command | a library path is invalid, or names std where a user library is required | use a lowercase path such as demo/tone; std is reserved |
| `CICADA-LIB-PRIVATE` | error | score | a score references a library declaration that is private | reference a public declaration of the library |
| `CICADA-LIB-REFERENCE` | error | score | a library reference does not name a declaration, uses a namespace no import binds, or a library parameter path lacks a direct import | import the library and reference namespace.name of a public declaration |
| `CICADA-LIB-ROOT` | error | command | scores in different folders keep separate library pins | run cicada lib update from each score's folder, or add a shared cicada.mod |
| `CICADA-LIB-SHADOW` | error | score | an import namespace collides with a declaration, another import or the reserved builtin namespace, or a library exists in more than one search location | rename the import or the declaration, or remove the duplicate library |
| `CICADA-LIB-SOURCE` | error | score | a library's source file cannot be read | restore the library's files or run cicada lib update |
| `CICADA-LIB-SUM` | error | score | cicada.sum is malformed | let cicada lib update rewrite it; each line is path std\|project\|user sha256:<64 hex digits> |
| `CICADA-LIMIT` | error | score, studio | a size or count limit is exceeded: name length, steps, tracks, voices, graph nodes, chain stages, image size, held inputs or source size | reduce what the message counts; cicada check --profile browser lists the portable limits |
| `CICADA-LIVE-ATTACK` | error | score | a live layers attack other than 1bar is given | use attack = 1bar |
| `CICADA-LIVE-BLOCK` | error | score | the live block is repeated, comes before a track, repeats a setting, or leaves an array implicit | write one live block after all tracks with each setting once |
| `CICADA-LIVE-COUNT-IN` | error | score | the live count_in is not 0 to 8 whole bars | use count_in = 0bars to 8bars |
| `CICADA-LIVE-LAND` | error | score | the live land value is unknown | use land = now, beat, bar, 2bars, 4bars or phrase |
| `CICADA-LIVE-LIMIT` | error | score | the live block has more than 16 macros, or layers use more than 3 distinct thresholds | remove macros or merge layer thresholds |
| `CICADA-LIVE-MACRO` | error | score | a live macro is duplicated, badly named, out of range, or maps to an invalid target | give each macro a unique 1 to 64 byte name, a unitless value from 0 to 1 and valid targets |
| `CICADA-LIVE-PHRASE` | error | score | the live phrase is not 1 to 64 bars | use phrase = 1bars to 64bars |
| `CICADA-LIVE-RECORD` | error | score | the live record division does not resolve to 30 to 3840 ticks | use a musical division such as 1/16 or 1bar |
| `CICADA-LIVE-RELEASE` | error | score | the live layers release is not 1 to 16 bars | use release = 1bars to 16bars |
| `CICADA-LIVE-TRACK` | error | score | a live layer rule names an unknown track or repeats one | name each declared track at most once |
| `CICADA-LOCKED` | error | edit | a phrase repair would need to change a locked step | unlock the step the message names, or edit the phrase directly |
| `CICADA-MANIFEST` | error | score | cicada.mod has an unknown, repeated or malformed directive | keep one project name and one supported cicada edition, with each directive once |
| `CICADA-MIDI` | error | score | the midi block is invalid: a port is unknown or repeated, a channel is outside 1 to 16, a note or controller outside 0 to 127, or a mapping target is invalid | declare each port once and map inputs to existing tracks, scenes and parameters |
| `CICADA-NOTE` | error | studio | a live note was refused: invalid input identity, note or velocity, or a voice without browser live notes | send a MIDI note 0 to 127 with velocity 1 to 127 to a track whose voice plays live |
| `CICADA-NOTES` | error | edit | an editnotes batch was refused because of one note; the reason and the note (at, step, pitch or lane) come as data | read reason and note in the error, then change the batch; docs/manual/editors.md describes each reason |
| `CICADA-PARAM` | error | score, command, studio | a parameter, attribute or setting is unknown, out of range, or not allowed here | check the name, range and unit with cicada params and cicada explain; the message names the value |
| `CICADA-PERFORMANCE` | error | score | a performance pattern is invalid: bad note fields, overlapping gates of one pitch, gesture times outside a note, or ticks outside a performance | give each note a MIDI pitch, velocity 1 to 127, start and length in ticks inside the loop, and gesture points inside its held length |
| `CICADA-POSITION` | error | score | a position is invalid or out of order: arrangement tempo steps, automation points or contour points | write positions as @bar.beat.step in increasing order inside the song; contours run from @0 to @1 |
| `CICADA-PRESET-PARAM` | error | score | a preset sets a parameter its target instrument does not have, or a structural one | set only the target's parameters (cicada explain lists them) |
| `CICADA-PRESET-RANGE` | error | score | a preset value is outside its parameter's range | use a value inside the range the message gives |
| `CICADA-PRESET-TARGET` | error | score | a preset's instrument target is missing or incompatible | set instrument = an existing instrument or built-in voice |
| `CICADA-PRESET-TYPE` | error | score | a preset value has the wrong type: not one of the allowed values, not on or off, not a finite number or not an integer | use a value of the type the message expects |
| `CICADA-PRESET-UNIT` | error | score | a preset value has the wrong unit | use the unit the message names |
| `CICADA-RATE` | error, warning | score | a modulator's rate is not what it plays: the warning when loop = continue fits whole cycles to the song at another rate, the error when a routed modulator exceeds 20 Hz at the song's fastest tempo | choose a rate that fits the song's length, or a slower one; the message gives the rate that plays |
| `CICADA-REFERENCE` | error | score | a name refers to nothing: an unknown track, pattern, scene, instrument, effect, bus, clip, asset or profile; close names get a spelling suggestion | declare it, or use one of the names the message suggests |
| `CICADA-REVISION` | error | studio | the public demo session changed since the client read it | refresh, then edit again |
| `CICADA-ROUTE` | error | score | a modulation route reaches a target it cannot modulate: a legacy effect setting, a non-track row, a non-continuous row, or an envelope's own input | route to a continuous live track mixer or voice parameter |
| `CICADA-ROW` | error | score | a velocity row is invalid: wrong length, a value outside 1 to 127, or a holding dot with no earlier value | give the row one entry per expanded step, values 1 to 127, and a value before the first dot |
| `CICADA-SAMPLER-MEMORY` | error | score, command | the sampler packs decode to more PCM than the resident cap allows | use smaller packs, or give a larger cap with --max-resident-pcm or CICADA_MAX_RESIDENT_PCM, such as 2GiB |
| `CICADA-SAMPLER-PACK` | error | score | a sampler pack is declared wrongly or does not load at 44.1, 48 or 96 kHz | declare a relative JSON pack with its SHA-256 pin and no asset or loop mode, and fix the pack the message names |
| `CICADA-SAMPLER-PARAM` | error | score | a sampler's fields are invalid: root, mode, voices, envelope or the field set | use an absolute root c0 to b6, mode oneshot or loop, voices 1 to 32 and valid envelope times |
| `CICADA-SAMPLER-ZONE` | error, warning | score | a note falls outside every zone of its sampler pack, or a hit velocity no zone covers (errors); a warning when a hit's velocity is outside the recorded range and plays at the nearest recorded one | move the note into the pack's key range, write it in another octave, change the pattern's transpose, or use a pack that covers it; for the warning, write a velocity the pack records |
| `CICADA-SCALE-DEGREE` | error | score | a scale degree does not exist in the score's scale (2 and 6 in pent and blues) | choose a degree in the scale or use an absolute letter pitch |
| `CICADA-SEED` | error | score | a seed is outside 0 to 4294967295 | use a seed from 0 to 4294967295 |
| `CICADA-SLIDE-REST` | warning | score | a slide leads into a rest, so it has no effect | slide into a note, or remove the slide |
| `CICADA-SOLO` | warning | score | a saved solo switch is on, so render and check play only the soloed parts | turn solo off before delivering, unless you mean it |
| `CICADA-SOURCE-MISSING` | error | score | a score that cicada.mod lists cannot be read | restore the file or remove it from cicada.mod |
| `CICADA-SOURCE-PATH` | error | score | a source path is absolute, uses traversal or patterns, is not listed in cicada.mod, or leaves the project | list project-relative .cicada paths in cicada.mod |
| `CICADA-SYNTAX` | error | score | the text does not parse: a token or declaration is malformed | check braces, spelling and separators near the position the message gives |
| `CICADA-UNIT` | error | score | a value has the wrong unit or type for its field | use the unit cicada explain gives for the field, such as Hz, ms, dB or bars |
| `CICADA-UNSUPPORTED` | error | score, command, studio | valid notation that the engine does not implement: a route, effect kind or placement, a setting without an engine representation, or an export option combination | use a supported alternative; the message names what is not implemented |
| `CICADA-USE` | error | score | a phrase use is invalid: repeat outside 1 to 64 or transpose outside -24 to 24 | use repeat 1 to 64 and transpose -24 to +24 |
| `CICADA-VERSION` | error | score, command, studio | the edition is unsupported, the score header and cicada.mod disagree, or a removed edition-1 spelling is used | run cicada fix to migrate legacy spellings (check --json offers it as a fix); keep the header and cicada.mod on one edition |

## CICADA-NOTES reasons

A `CICADA-NOTES` refusal carries one of these values in `reason`.

| `reason` | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `invalid-note` | the note has a start, length, pitch or velocity outside its range |
| `note-changed` | the note is missing, or its length or velocity differs; read the pattern again |
| `no-lanes` | the batch names a lane in a pattern without drum lanes |
| `not-whole-steps` | the note does not start or end on the pattern's step grid |
| `outside-pattern` | the note would leave the pattern's steps |
| `outside-lanes` | the note would leave the pattern's lanes |
| `outside-loop` | the note would leave the performance loop |
| `pitch-range` | the note would leave MIDI 0 to 127, counting the pattern's transpose |
| `too-short` | the note would become shorter than one step or one tick |
| `gesture-cut` | the note would end before its last gesture point |
| `overlap` | the note would overlap another note: the same pitch in a performance, or any note in a step pattern |
| `same-pitch` | the note would land on the pitch of another selected note |
| `same-cell` | the note would land on the drum cell of another selected note |
| `chord-pitches-equal` | the note would equal another pitch of its own chord |
| `chord-size` | the note would make a chord of more than four pitches |
| `chord-articulation` | the note would make a chord with a note that slides or ratchets |
| `chord-length` | the note would join a chord of another length |
| `chord-modifiers` | the note would join a chord with another accent, chance or velocity |
| `acid-one-pitch` | the note would put a second pitch on an acid step |
| `fixed-length` | the note is a drum hit, which lasts one step |
| `unknown-lane` | the note names a drum lane the pattern does not have |

# docs/manual/troubleshooting.md

# Troubleshooting

Start with the command that reports the source location and stable diagnostic:

```sh
cicada check
cicada check main.cicada
cicada validate main.cicada
```

`check` validates all scores under the nearest `cicada.mod`. `validate` checks
one score. Both parse and compile the project; a score can be grammatically
valid but still fail a name, type, unit, range, or engine check.

## Notation errors

Every code, with its meaning and fix, is in [Diagnostic codes](docs/manual/diagnostics.md);
`cicada diagnostics <code>` prints one. The most common:

- **`CICADA-SYNTAX`** — check braces, spelling, separators, and whether the
  construct exists in edition 2; see the [language reference](docs/spec/README.md).
- **`CICADA-REFERENCE`** — check that a track, pattern, scene, instrument, kit,
  or phrase name exists and is spelled consistently.
- **`CICADA-PARAM`** or **`CICADA-UNIT`** — check the field's range and unit in
  the [edition-1 reference](docs/spec/edition-1.md). For example, frequency uses
  `Hz` or `kHz` and time uses `ms` or `s`.
- **`CICADA-SCALE-DEGREE`** — degrees 2 and 6 are not part of the `pent` or
  `blues` scale. Use 1, 3, 4, 5, or 7, or choose another scale.
- **`CICADA-SLIDE-REST`** — a slide has no adjacent playable target. Check the
  next cell, pattern loop, and any scene switch that should provide the note.
- **Too many or mismatched steps** — each pitch pattern has 1–64 expanded
  cells; drum rows in a pattern must have equal lengths. A declared `steps`
  value is a check and must match the expanded pattern.
- **`CICADA-SAMPLER-ZONE`** — a note falls outside every zone of its track's
  sampler pack. `cicada check` shows the note's place in the source, its track
  and pattern, and the keys the pack covers. A note that a phrase supplies is
  shown at the `use`, with the phrase's name and the use's transpose. Move the
  note, write it in another octave, change the pattern's `transpose`, or use a
  pack that covers it. The sampler's `root` moves only a pitch written without
  an octave. Without the check, the render stops with engine fault 29.
- **`CICADA-SAMPLER-PACK`** — a pack does not load: its manifest or an audio
  file is missing or damaged, the manifest differs from the `sha256` pin in
  the `sampler` declaration, or the pack cannot play at 44.1, 48 or 96 kHz (the
  message then says `at 96000 Hz`). Build the pack again, or update the pin if
  you changed the pack on purpose. Pack paths are relative to the project
  folder, the one that holds `cicada.mod`.
- **`CICADA-SAMPLER-MEMORY`** — the packs of the score declare more decoded
  audio than the cap allows, so `render`, `stems` and `play` would refuse it.
  Use smaller packs or raise the cap; see the next section.

## Sampler packs use too much memory

- **`sampler packs exceed the native resident PCM cap`** — the packs of a
  `render`, `stems`, `audition`, `play` or Studio session would decode to more
  audio than the cap allows, 1 GiB by default. The message gives the cap and the
  size. It comes before any audio is read. Raise the cap, for example
  `cicada render song.cicada -o song.wav --max-resident-pcm 2GiB`, or
  `cicada studio --max-resident-pcm 2GiB`, or set `CICADA_MAX_RESIDENT_PCM=2GiB`
  where a command cannot take the option, or use smaller packs.
  `cicada check --max-resident-pcm 2GiB` checks against the same cap.
- **`project audio exceeds the 64 MiB resident PCM budget`** — sampler assets
  and clips held in memory together, or the packs and assets of a browser image
  or WAM2 export, pass 64 MiB. A native render does not count packs in this
  budget. For a browser score, use a smaller pack; see
  [instrument packs](docs/sampler/packs.md#memory-limits).

## Browser export is refused

A score can pass `cicada check` against the desktop limits (64 tracks, 256
voices) and still be refused for a browser image. Run
`cicada check --profile browser` to see which limit it reaches. The report lists
the voices each track reserves.

- **`portable browser/WAM exports support at most 16 tracks and 32 allocated
  voices`** — remove or merge tracks, or lower `voices` on keys tracks and
  sampler packs.
- **`project image exceeds 2 MiB`** or **`project image exceeds limit`** — the
  image stores audio at 4 bytes per sample per channel. Shorten or remove audio
  assets and samples. The report shows the audio as `image at least N of
  2097152 bytes`; the whole image is that size or larger.
- **`prepared master processor must be loaded separately`** — a browser image
  cannot carry a `master` insert. The `bus music` insert takes one compressor and
  no other effect, so put a compressor there and move any other effect to a track
  insert, which processes only that track. A track insert makes the image need
  the processing kernel `cicada-vocals.wasm`; see the
  [mix chain](docs/audio/mix-chain.md).

## Studio does not start

- **`GoSX workstation executable is missing`** — Studio runs as two programs,
  `cicada` and `cicada-workstation` (`cicada-workstation.exe` on Windows).
  `cicada studio` looks for the workstation next to `cicada`, then on `PATH`.
  `go build ./cmd/cicada` builds only `cicada`. From the repository root, run
  `make build`, then start Studio with `./build/cicada studio main.cicada`;
  both programs are in `build/`. If you move `cicada`, move
  `cicada-workstation` and the `workstation` folder with it, because the
  workstation reads its browser files from that folder. The VS Code extension
  needs the same files, so set `cicada.serverPath` to the absolute path of
  `build/cicada`.

## Studio or editor does not update

- If a source save is rejected, read the status line. Studio validates before
  writing; correct the error or discard the draft.
- If Studio says the file changed on disk, reload the page and combine your
  changes with the external edit before trying again.
- If the LSP does not start, confirm that `cicada lsp` runs in a terminal and
  that your editor launches the correct binary. In VS Code, set
  `cicada.serverPath` when the executable is not on `PATH`.
- When Studio is open beside VS Code, save one editor at a time. Studio and
  the extension exchange changes through the score file.
- Windows Studio needs a filesystem that supports its atomic replacement
  operation. A WSL UNC share can report `ReplaceFileW: The request is not
  supported`; the score remains unchanged. Run Studio inside WSL for that
  checkout, or use a Windows filesystem for a native Windows score.

## No sound or unexpected sound

- On Windows, Linux, and macOS, `cicada play` and Studio use Tymbal by default: WASAPI
  on Windows, ALSA on Linux, and CoreAudio on macOS. If Tymbal cannot open a device, Cicada names it
  and suggests `--audio oto`. On Linux, no ALSA default device or a device held
  by PipeWire or Pulse can cause this error. Use `--audio oto` or set
  `CICADA_AUDIO=oto` to select Oto explicitly. Use `--audio null` for real-time
  transport without an output device. Oto does not support microphone recording.
- On Mac, enable input in Audio and allow Cicada Studio under **System Settings →
  Privacy & Security → Microphone**. If a saved device was disconnected, refresh
  devices and reconnect it or choose a replacement. See the [Mac setup guide](docs/manual/macos.md).
- To check a score without live playback, render a WAV.
- If WSL has no ALSA playback device, use a native Windows build with Tymbal
  and WASAPI to audition the instruments. Keep its editable score on a Windows
  filesystem, as described above.
- If playback continues after an invalid save, Studio or `play` is keeping the
  last valid compiled score. Correct the reported diagnostic and save again.
- If a scene sounds incomplete, check that each track has a compatible
  pattern assignment. A missing track assignment means keep its previous
  pattern; it does not mean stop.
- If a sound is too quiet or clips, inspect track levels and the render summary.
  `--normalize` sets the file's sample peak; it does not balance the mix or
  control perceived loudness.

## Export problems

- A stem export's destination directory must not already exist. Choose a new
  name, then run `verify-stems` on the completed directory.
- When checking a WAV range, pass the same `--from`, `--bars`, and `--tail`
  values to `verify-wav` that you used for `render`. Bar numbers start at 1;
  `--from 1` selects the first bar. The old `--from 0` input still selects bar
  1 and prints a deprecation warning.
- MIDI chance output is deterministic: the exporter uses the first seeded
  pass on each repetition. It does not encode a live probability generator.
- If a typed JSON field is rejected, inspect the public schema and field
  catalog using `cicada fields` or the links in
  [Semantic JSON](docs/spec/semantic-model.md#semantic-json).

# docs/cli.md

# CLI reference

Run `cicada help` for the command list, `cicada help COMMAND` for command usage,
or `cicada help lib COMMAND` for a library subcommand. Each command also accepts
`--help`.

## Audition

`cicada audition SCORE [-o DIR] [--from BAR] [--bars N] [--json]` renders the
mix and stems and reports the heard key, written and heard chords per bar,
per-track level, brightness, attack, decay and rhythm, and per-section
loudness. With `-o` it writes `spectrogram.png`, `chroma.png` and
`rhythm.png`. See [Audition](docs/manual/audition.md) for each field and the JSON
schema.

## Sampler pack memory

`cicada render SCORE -o FILE`, `cicada stems SCORE -o DIR`, `cicada play
[SCORE]`, `cicada audition SCORE`, `cicada check [SCORE]` and `cicada studio
[SCORE]` take `--max-resident-pcm SIZE`. It caps the decoded PCM of all sampler
packs the score loads, 1 GiB by default. When the option is omitted, the
environment variable `CICADA_MAX_RESIDENT_PCM` sets the cap, which is how to
give Studio another cap when it starts from a launcher that passes no flags.
SIZE is a whole number with a unit: `KiB`, `MiB`, `GiB` or `TiB`, or `KB`, `MB`,
`GB` or `TB`, in capitals or in lower case (`Mb` is refused, because it can
read as megabits). The cap is counted from the pack manifests before any audio
is read, so a score over the cap is refused without allocating its audio, and
the message names the cap and the size. `cicada check` reports the same
refusal as `CICADA-SAMPLER-MEMORY`, loads the packs one at a time, and reports a
pack that does not load at 44.1, 48 or 96 kHz and a note outside every zone of
its pack. See [instrument packs](docs/sampler/packs.md#memory-limits).

```sh
cicada render song.cicada -o song.wav --max-resident-pcm 2GiB
```

## CPU profiles

`cicada render`, `cicada stems`, `cicada apply`, `cicada check` and `cicada
audition` take `--cpuprofile FILE`. The command writes a standard Go CPU
profile of its whole run to FILE, also when it fails (a loudness shortfall
included), and its other output does not change. Read the profile with `go tool
pprof`:

```sh
cicada render song.cicada -o song.wav --loudness -14 --cpuprofile render.prof
go tool pprof -top render.prof
```

## Loudness targets and repeated renders

`cicada render --loudness` searches for the export gain in up to six passes.
The first pass synthesizes the song; every later pass replays that pass's mix
from a temporary file next to the output (8 bytes per frame, about 71 MB for a
three-minute song at 48 kHz) and runs only the master stage, the measurement
and the WAV writing again. A pass whose gain would not change the audio is not
rendered at all. The output and the reported numbers are byte for byte those of
a search that synthesizes every pass. The summary line counts the passes by how
they got their audio, and one line per pass gives its gain, loudness and true
peak:

```text
song.wav: 40 bars from bar 1, 4574770 frames at 48000 Hz, achieved -15.05 LUFS, true peak -1.05 dBTP, applied gain +11.41 dB, DC correction L +0.0000000/R +0.0000000 FS, passes 2 (full syntheses 1, cached replays 1, repeats 0), largest limiter gain reduction 0.00 dB
song.wav: pass 1: gain +0.00 dB, -26.45 LUFS, true peak -12.46 dBTP, synthesized
song.wav: pass 2: gain +11.41 dB, -15.05 LUFS, true peak -1.05 dBTP, replayed
```

`render --json` reports the same counts and passes (see
[Agents and JSON output](docs/manual/agents.md#render---json)). `--normalize` renders
twice in the same way: its second render replays the first one's mix. When the
temporary file cannot be written, for example on a full disk, every render runs
in full.

Set `CICADA_RENDER_NO_REUSE=1` to turn all reuse off: every loudness pass and
both normalization renders synthesize the song in full, and the counts show
only syntheses. The output must be the same byte for byte; the variable is
there to work around a difference you find, and to show whether reuse caused
it.

```sh
CICADA_RENDER_NO_REUSE=1 cicada render song.cicada -o song.wav --loudness -14
```

On Linux and macOS the stored mix has no name in the folder, so its space
returns however the render ends. On Windows it keeps its name until the render
ends. If a render is interrupted (Ctrl-C), it removes its temporary files
before it exits; files that a killed render leaves behind (names that start
with `.cicada-render-`, `.cicada-loudness-` or `.cicada-master-cache-`) are
removed by the next render in that folder once they are a day old.

## Libraries

Run library commands from the project folder, except `new`, which needs no
project. Library paths use slash-separated namespace identifiers.

| Command | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `cicada lib list` | List available embedded, project, and user libraries with their resolution kinds. Includes duplicate paths; does not change pins. |
| `cicada lib show PATH` | Print the resolved manifest, declarations, audio paths, SHA-256 hash, and resolution directory. Does not change pins. |
| `cicada lib new PATH [--dir DIR]` | Create an edition-2 manifest and starter source in the user library. `--dir` selects a directory while keeping the library path. Absolute or dot-prefixed `PATH` selects a directory and uses its final name. Refuses existing destinations and the `std` namespace. |
| `cicada lib update [PATH]` | Accept current bytes and resolution kind for one imported library, or all imports when omitted. Prints old/new pins; removes unused pins when updating all. |
| `cicada lib vendor` | Verify pins, stage and verify imported user libraries in project `lib/`, and publish project pins. Includes transitive imports; refuses different existing libraries. |

`CICADA_LIBRARY` overrides the default user config directory's `cicada/lib`
folder. Library identity uses hashes; remote fetching and version requirements
are not supported. See [Managing libraries](docs/manual/libraries.md) for examples
and pinning behavior.

## Save As

`cicada save-as SCORE TARGET` copies the score, project sources, audio,
retained takes, history, and imported libraries. It automatically vendors user
and project libraries and writes target pins before publishing the score.
Dependencies with different content and existing target scores are refused.
Studio Save As uses the same operation.

`cicada bundle SCORE OUTPUT.zip` creates a portable ZIP containing the Save As
copy and a `cicada-bundle.json` inventory of file hashes and bundled library
identities. It refuses an existing output. Retained takes and recovery files
are included and may contain unpublished work; see [Managing libraries](docs/manual/libraries.md)
for their portability limits. After extraction, run
`cicada bundle --restore-history main.cicada` to attach inventoried recovery
versions without overwriting different files.

## Inspect a musical moment

`cicada explain SCORE PATH @bar[.beat[.step]]` reports the parameter's default,
preset and track overrides, inherited scene setting, and active song automation.
The computed value includes the automation lane once it reaches its first point;
the lane holds its last value and takes precedence over later scene settings.
Positions use 4/4: bars start at 1, and beat and sixteenth values are 1–4.

```sh
cicada explain examples/songs/neon-causeway.cicada bass.cutoff @15
cicada explain examples/songs/neon-causeway.cicada bass.cutoff @17
```

The first command inspects the build; the second reaches its 2200 Hz target.
Reported automation values are float32 control targets; audio smoothing can lag
the target. Named-placement arrangements support parameter inspection within
their whole-bar export span; their live scene definitions do not contribute
settings to the arrangement.
